At that time, he was 12 years, 4 months, and 25 days old. With this, he broke the 19-year-old record of Russian Sergey Karjakin (12 years 7 months) and became the youngest Grandmaster in chess history. Thus, Statement II is factually correct.

However, as per the UPSC Provisional Answer Key, the correct answer has been given as "1 and 2 only. Statement 3 is incorrect: No rule limits the number of wild cards an individual player may receive across Grand Slam tournaments. Wild cards are given at each organiser's discretion. • Note: It is neither practical nor necessary for an aspirant to know every such highly specific, obscure information.
